answers.answer: In SCOPe 2.08 all three structures sit in the same place: a.47.2.1 (class a, All alpha; fold a.47 STAT-like; superfamily a.47.2 t-snare proteins; family a.47.2.1 t-snare proteins). 1br0 chain A (d1br0a_, sunid 17772) and 1ez3 chains A, B and C (d1ez3a_, d1ez3b_, d1ez3c_) are in the 'Syntaxin 1A N-terminal domain' protein node (rat). 1dn1 chain B (d1dn1b_, sunid 302344) is the full-length domain, in the same family under the 'automated matches' protein node, with the comment 'automated match to d3c98b_'. 1dn1 is obsolete, superseded by 3c98, and chain A (d1dn1a_) is the Sec1/Munc18 partner (e.200s-style e.25.1.1), a separate domain. So SCOPe does not treat the fragment structures as a different fold or as unclassifiable. The fragment entries d1br0a_ and d1ez3a_ carry the comment 'three-helical fragment; similar to one spectrin repeat'. They also carry the inconsistency flag 'ms': missing some secondary structures that made up less than one-third of the common domain. Biological interpretation: (1) The fold assignment for the fragments is a placement of an incomplete piece. Three helices are enough to be recognized as STAT-like/spectrin-repeat-like helical bundle architecture, but they are not the complete domain. The full domain, as in 1dn1 chain B, is the reference for what the domain is, including its fourth helix and its context. (2) The fragment-based fold assignment should not be read as a new fold, a distinct domain, or a different family. It is evidence only for the shared three-helix core. The 'ms' flag marks the entry as an incomplete representative, and it is not evidence of a different evolutionary origin. (3) Fold-level similarity (a.47 STAT-like, with spectrin-repeat resemblance) is not by itself homology. Homology is asserted only at the superfamily/family levels (a.47.2 / a.47.2.1), supported by the full-domain structures and the t-snare relationship. The spectrin-repeat comment is only a structural similarity note. (4) Do not transfer function, boundaries, or templates from fragment domains. Use full-domain representatives such as d1dn1b_ (or the d3c98b_ match) for modeling the whole N-terminal domain, and treat fragment entries as partial and as incomplete for boundary definition, interface or Sec1-binding analysis, and domain-count inferences. Automated-match nodes are also not curated protein-level assignments, so the distinction between the curated 'Syntaxin 1A N-terminal domain' protein node and the 'automated matches' node should not be over-read as a biological difference. Caveat: I did not retrieve earlier SCOPe releases, so I cannot state from this evidence how these entries were classified historically; the statement above describes the current 2.08 treatment only.
